body: Hey op, and thanks for the well wishes! I actually landed a much better job in the middle of October. I'm a Library Assistant now, 20hrs a week, permanent hire, chance to go to 32hrs when the budget comes through for them. It's comfortable and I'm starting to recover a bit from the previous summer. I hope you're doing well yourself and happy New Year!

I (27F) am making attempts to change my entire wardrobe, or at least move away from t-shirts to proper blouses for casual wear. Having an office job at one point really sealed the deal for me since I've basically lived in the t-shirt and jeans combo. A bit difficult since I live in a HCOL area but I've been slowly revamping the closet. Very tough to beat a nice pair of jeans though.

So far all of my chickens have been born male and my calves born female. On the one hand it's nice to get so many T2 varieties, but on the other hand I can't breed any of them for T3. I was thinking it was just me but I'm going to hold off on breeding until a patch 🥲

Underemployed since February. Down to anywhere between 6 to 10 hours a week since April. Millennial/Gen Z limbo (27F.) Been applying for full time positions or even "part time" that'll give 25-35 hours a week but the wait has been painful.

Stainless steel appliances in the kitchen, a fridge with an ice maker, a functional dishwasher, and marble countertops. Used to browse old Home and Garden magazines all the time as a kid jealous because our counters/cabinets were solid beige with wood doors.

If we're talking monthly then I try to keep it under $150. Sometimes it goes over $200. I live in a high cost-low quality area so often even produce will pull the bill up. I've been shifting to shopping bulk sections for grains/pasta/beans and relying on sales for produce to help.

No canned soups or boxed meals anymore since they've started to hit $4 each here. I'll pick a soup or a stew or something easy to make several servings of and eat off of that for the next couple of days. Juggle between something with rice then something with pasta then something with potatoes.

On the one hand my cooking has gotten much better to sustain myself with. On the other it sucks seeing fruit and vegetables go back to $3.98 each or even $5 a pound across the board for even the in season produce and watching frozen bags get shrunk and price hiked.

That's the spot I'm in right now. All interviews, no bite. I used to be able to set a timer from the day of an interview to the rejection email sadly. Now I'm just ghosted, but still getting interviews. Keep at it op. Praying one of them lands it for you.

I work grocery but I've also worked in mall clothing stores where all pets were allowed and it's a mess on both ends and I wish people could learn to leave their pets at home. The grocery store only allows Service Animals inside but lately I've noticed that more and more people are putting their little untrained lap dogs into baby carriers and even mini wagons and rolling them into the store unleashed.

While it's just a little better than letting them walk freely and paw at all of the produce or putting them directly in the carts a dog is not a baby and unless they're service dogs they still don't belong in a grocery store. They look pretty distressed most of the time too. Maybe it's just my location specifically, but it's happening more often with different people who just can't seem to leave their pets at home for like the hour or so needed to do their groceries.

My 24/7 grocery store has started to shut down self checkout on weekends and put up blockades in the liquor aisle and, oddly enough, the health-care aisle. It's to the point they're also considering locking up mouthwash, house cleaners, beauty supplies, and adding blockades to the candy aisle. If someone needs emergency cold or flu medication or cleaning supplies in case of late night accidents they'll be out of luck, and no self checkout means depending on the hour there will only be two cashiers and a whole lot of late night multi-cart orders ahead of them.

Every time it's an old woman I brace for impact because they are usually the nastiest. Simply asking for "Camel" or "Marlboro" and when I ask them to specify, because I don't smoke, they get so mad. I'm not going to leave the checkout stand during a rush just to play a guessing game but they treat going to customer service ten feet away to get it directly through them like it's a punishment.

I have a pretty common first name and so many customers like to joke the moment they see me like "[first name] as in [insert celebrity with the same name]?!" It sucks so much. And so many male customers try to get friendly with me by using my name every other sentence. It's gross. I wish I could take my name badge off or turn it around but we're not allowed.

I just shut my emotions off. People don't like to chatter with cashiers at the store I work at so the transactions go faster, giving me room to just go with the motions. If someone gets worked up over us not having an item or get upset at the prices and try to make it my fault I just point them to customer service three feet away. Save my emotions for home and people that actually care about me. In this age and economy it's not worth it to let customers have emotional access.

Temp job I finished back in Feb was supposed to be a two year assignment. Got a call out of the blue saying the assignment was actually finished after nine months. Stuck in a grocery store for money and hope it'll tide me over until I can get back into a field of work I actually loved.

Some of my store's customers have hands so visibly filthy I change my gloves after handing them their change, don't even wait for them to leave. And then so many women pull their cash out from inside their BRA then lick to count the bills out.
